subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions. Learn the zero, first, second and third conditionals, and never put will after if.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন। zero, first, second আর third conditional শেখো, আর if-এর পরে কখনো will নয়।

rule.en: Use if + present, present for things that are always true, like facts of science.
rule.bn: যা সবসময় সত্য, যেমন বিজ্ঞানের তথ্য, তার জন্য if + present, present।

recap.example: If you heat ice, it melts.

questions.prompt: If you mix red and white, you ___ pink.

options.why: This is always true, so use the present, not the past.
After will, use the base verb. And facts use the present anyway.
The verb needs a tense: get.

questions.explanation: Always true: if + present, present.

questions.prompt: Water ___ if you heat it to 100°C.

options.why: Water is singular, so add -s: boils.
This is always true, so use the present.
would is for imagined things, but this is a fact.

questions.explanation: Fact: present simple, boils.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a zero conditional?

options.text: If you heat butter, it will melt.
options.why: That is a first conditional (will).

options.text: If you heated butter, it would melt.
options.why: That is a second conditional (past + would).

options.text: If you heat butter, it melts.
If you had heated butter, it would have melted.
options.why: That is a third conditional.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional: the present in both parts.

rule.en: Use if + present, will + verb for a real or likely future. Never put will after if.
rule.bn: বাস্তব বা সম্ভাব্য ভবিষ্যতের জন্য if + present, will + verb। if-এর পরে কখনো will বসবে না।

recap.example: If it rains, I’ll stay at home.

questions.prompt: If you study, you ___.

options.why: would is for imagined things. This future is real.
This is about the future, so use will pass.
After will, use the base verb: pass.

questions.explanation: Real future result: will + verb.

questions.prompt: If she ___ tomorrow, we will go out.

options.why: Never put will after if. Use the present: comes.
With she, add -s: comes.
came is past. For a real future, use the present after if.

questions.explanation: if + present (comes), will + verb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: If it will rain, I will stay at home.
options.why: Never put will after if.

options.text: If it rain, I will stay at home.
options.why: With it, add -s: rains.

options.text: If it rains, I will stay at home.
If it rains, I would stay at home.
options.why: A real future uses will, not would.

questions.explanation: if + present, will + verb.

rule.en: unless means if not. After unless, when and as soon as, use the present to talk about the future.
rule.bn: unless মানে if not। unless, when, as soon as-এর পরে ভবিষ্যৎ বোঝাতেও present ব্যবহার করো।

recap.example: Unless you hurry, you’ll miss the bus. · I’ll call when I arrive.

questions.prompt: ___ you hurry, you’ll be late.

options.why: “If you hurry, you’ll be late” makes no sense. You mean if you don’t hurry.
“When you hurry, you’ll be late” makes no sense.
Hurrying doesn’t make you late. You need “if not”.

questions.explanation: Unless = if not: if you don’t hurry, you’ll be late.

questions.prompt: I’ll text you as soon as I ___ home.

options.why: No will after as soon as. Use the present.
This is about the future, so use the present after as soon as.
The verb needs a tense: reach.

questions.explanation: as soon as + present, for the future.

questions.prompt: “If you don’t water the plant, it will die.” Which means the same?

options.text: Unless you don’t water the plant, it will die.
options.why: unless already means if not. Don’t add another not.

options.text: Unless you will water the plant, it will die.
options.why: No will after unless.

options.text: Unless you water the plant, it will die.
Unless you water the plant, it won’t die.
options.why: This means the opposite.

questions.explanation: if … don’t = unless.

rule.en: Use if + past simple, would + verb for things that are not true now or are unlikely. With I, he and she, we often use were.
rule.bn: যা এখন সত্য নয় বা ঘটার সম্ভাবনা কম, তার জন্য if + past simple, would + verb। I, he, she-এর সাথেও প্রায়ই were বসে।

recap.example: If I had wings, I would fly.

questions.prompt: If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.

options.why: am is the real present. This is imagined, so use the past: were.
Never put will after if.
would goes in the result, not after if.

questions.explanation: Imagined now: if + were, would + verb.

questions.prompt: If he knew the answer, he ___ us.

options.why: knew is past, so this is imagined: would, not will.
The result needs would: would tell.
After would, use the base verb: tell.

questions.explanation: if + past, would + base verb.

questions.prompt: “I don’t have a car, so I don’t drive to work.” Which means the same?

options.text: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
If I have a car, I will drive to work.
options.why: This sounds like you might get a car. In fact, you don’t have one.

options.text: If I would have a car, I would drive to work.
options.why: No would after if.

options.text: If I had a car, I drive to work.
options.why: The result needs would: would drive.

questions.explanation: Not true now → if + past, would + verb.

rule.en: Use If I were you, I would (I’d) + verb to give advice. Use were in this phrase.
rule.bn: পরামর্শ দিতে If I were you, I would (I’d) + verb। এই বাক্যে were বসে।

recap.example: If I were you, I’d apologise.

questions.prompt: If I ___ you, I’d see a doctor.

options.why: You can’t really be the other person, so use the imagined form: were.
Never put will after if.
The verb needs the past form: were.

questions.explanation: Fixed phrase: If I were you.

questions.prompt: If I were you, I ___ that phone. It’s too expensive.

options.why: This is imagined, so use wouldn’t, not won’t.
After wouldn’t, use the base verb: buy.
The result needs would: wouldn’t buy.

questions.explanation: If I were you, I wouldn’t + verb = advice not to.

questions.prompt: “You should save money.” Which gives the same advice?

options.text: If I am you, I will save money.
options.why: Use the imagined form: If I were you, I would.

options.text: If I were you, I would save money.
If I were you, I will save money.
options.why: were goes with would, not will.

options.text: If you were me, I would save money.
options.why: The words are swapped. Say If I were you.

questions.explanation: If I were you, I would + verb = you should.

rule.en: If something is possible or likely, use if + present, will. If it is imagined or unlikely, use if + past, would.
rule.bn: সম্ভব বা সম্ভাব্য হলে if + present, will। কাল্পনিক বা অসম্ভাব্য হলে if + past, would।

recap.example: If I pass, I’ll celebrate. · If I won the lottery, I’d buy a house.

questions.prompt: If I ___ a crore taka in the lottery, I’d buy a flat.

options.why: I’d (I would) shows this is imagined, so use the past: won.
Never put will after if.
No would after if.

questions.explanation: Unlikely → if + past, would.

questions.prompt: If the shop is open, I ___ some bread.

options.why: “is open” is real and likely, so use will.
This is about the future, so use will buy.
After will, use the base verb: buy.

questions.explanation: Likely → if + present, will.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: If I see Nila tomorrow, I would tell her.
options.why: see (present) goes with will, not would.

options.text: If I see Nila tomorrow, I will tell her.
If I will see Nila tomorrow, I will tell her.
options.why: Never put will after if.

options.text: If I saw Nila tomorrow, I will tell her.
options.why: saw (past) goes with would, not will.

questions.explanation: A real plan: if + present, will.

cards.badge: If + had + V3, would have + V3

rule.en: Use if + had + V3, would have + V3 to imagine a different past: something that did not happen.
rule.bn: অতীতে যা ঘটেনি, তা কল্পনা করতে if + had + V3, would have + V3।

recap.example: If I had studied, I would have passed.

questions.prompt: If we had left earlier, we ___ the train.

options.why: This is about the past, so use would have + V3.
After have, use V3: caught.
Use would, not will, for an imagined past.

questions.explanation: if + had + V3, would have + V3.

questions.prompt: If she ___ about the party, she would have come.

options.why: This is about the past, so use had + V3.
No would after if.
Use had, not has, for the imagined past.

questions.explanation: if + had + V3.

questions.prompt: “I didn’t set an alarm, so I woke up late.” Which means the same?

options.text: If I had set an alarm, I wouldn’t have woken up late.
If I set an alarm, I won’t wake up late.
options.why: This is about the future, but the story is in the past.

options.text: If I had set an alarm, I wouldn’t wake up late.
options.why: The result is in the past too: wouldn’t have woken.

options.text: If I would have set an alarm, I wouldn’t have woken up late.
options.why: No would after if.

questions.explanation: Imagined past: if + had + V3, wouldn’t have + V3.

rule.en: When a past action changes the present, use if + had + V3, would + verb.
rule.bn: অতীতের কোনো কাজের ফল এখন দেখা গেলে if + had + V3, would + verb।

recap.example: If I had eaten breakfast, I wouldn’t be hungry now.

questions.prompt: If I had taken that job, I ___ rich now.

options.why: This is imagined, so use would.
The result needs would: would be.
“now” shows a present result: would be.

questions.explanation: Past cause, present result: would + verb.

questions.prompt: If she ___ the bus, she would be here now.

options.why: Missing the bus happened in the past, so use had + V3.
No would after if.
Use had, not has.

questions.explanation: Past cause: if + hadn’t + V3.

questions.prompt: “I didn’t learn to swim as a child, so I can’t swim now.” Which means the same?

options.text: If I learnt to swim as a child, I can swim now.
options.why: Past + can doesn’t work here. Use had learnt … could.

options.text: If I had learnt to swim as a child, I could have swum now.
options.why: “now” needs a present result: could swim.

options.text: If I had learnt to swim as a child, I could swim now.
If I would have learnt to swim as a child, I could swim now.
options.why: No would after if.

questions.explanation: if + had + V3, could/would + verb (now).
